children.name: Ammotragus
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the aoudad or Barbary sheep, a large, shaggy-legged wild caprid native to North Africa's rocky mountains, now introduced and thriving in feral populations across the American Southwest and southern Europe.

children.name: Ammotragus lervia
children.description: The Barbary sheep (Ammotragus lervia), also known as aoudad (pronounced [ˈɑʊdæd]), is a species of caprine native to rocky mountains in North Africa and parts of West Africa.

children.name: Arabitragus
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Arabian tahr, the smallest and most endangered tahr species, clinging to the rocky escarpments and cliffs of Oman's Hajar Mountains.

children.name: Arabitragus jayakari
children.description: The Arabian tahr (Arabitragus jayakari) is a species of tahr native to eastern Arabia.

children.name: Budorcas
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the takin, a massive, thick-set caprid of Himalayan and Chinese mountain forests with a unique moose-like face, thought by some to be the origin of the 'Golden Fleece' legend.

children.name: Budorcas bedfordi
children.description: Budorcas bedfordi (Golden Takin) is a takin species found in Asia region.

children.name: Budorcas taxicolor
children.description: The takin (Budorcas taxicolor);  is a large species of ungulate of the subfamily Caprinae found in the eastern Himalayas..

children.name: Budorcas tibetana
children.description: The Sichuan takin or Tibetan takin (Budorcas taxicolor tibetana) is a subspecies of takin (goat-antelope).

children.name: Budorcas whitei
children.description: Budorcas whitei (White's Takin) is a takin species found in Asia region.

children.name: Capra
children.description: The true wild goats and ibexes, around nine species of sure-footed mountain caprids distributed from Western Europe to the Himalayas, including the bezoar ibex ancestor of all domestic goats.

children.name: Capra aegagrus
children.description: The wild goat (Capra aegagrus) is a goat species, inhabiting forests, shrublands and rocky areas ranging from Turkey and the Caucasus in the west to Iran, Turkmenistan, Afghanistan, and Pakistan in the east.

children.name: Capra caucasica
children.description: The West Caucasian tur (Capra caucasica) is a mountain-dwelling goat-antelope native to the western half of the Caucasus Mountains range, in Georgia and European Russia..

children.name: Capra cylindricornis
children.description: The East Caucasian tur (Capra cylindricornis) is a mountain-dwelling caprine living in the eastern half of the Greater Caucasus mountains, in Azerbaijan, Georgia, and European Russia..

children.name: Capra falconeri
children.description: The markhor (Capra falconeri)  is a large wild Capra species native to the mountain regions at the crossroads of Central and South Asia, including the Karakoram and Himalayas..

children.name: Capra hircus
Alpine
children.description:
The Alpine is a medium to large sized breed of domestic goat known for its very good milking ability. They have no set colours or markings (although certain markings are discriminated against). They have horns, a straight profile and erect ears.
The breed originated in the French Alps. Mature goats weigh around 61 kg (135 lbs), and are about 76 cm (30 in) tall at the shoulder. Alpine goats can range from white or gray to brown and black. Alpine goats are heavy milkers. The milk can be made into butter, cheese, soap, ice cream or any other dairy product normally made from cow's milk. They are often used for commercial dairy production, as well as homestead milk goats.

children.name: LaMancha
children.description:
American Lamancha, or more commonly, simply Lamancha or LaMancha goat, is a formally recognized breed of dairy goat, first bred in California by Mrs. Eula Fay Frey about 1927. Later she moved the herd to Glide, Oregon for further development. The Lamancha goat is a member of the Capra genus, specifically Capra aegagrus hircus (sometimes called Capra hircus), like all domestic goats.
Lamancha goats are perhaps the most distinctive goat breed; easily recognizable by their very short ear pinnae. They are also known for their high milk production, and the comparatively high butterfat content in their milk, and people-loving temperament. The short-eared American Lamanchas first gained recognition as a distinct breed in the early 1950s, and the breed was registered formally on January 27, 1958 as "Lamancha or American Lamancha" goats. Approximately 200 animals were accepted at registration as its original stock. The first true American Lamancha goat registered was named Fay's Ernie, L-1.

children.name: Nubian
children.description: The Anglo-Nubian is a British breed of domestic goat. It originated in the nineteenth century from cross-breeding between native British goats and a mixed population of large lop-eared goats imported from India, the Middle East and North Africa. It is characterised by large, pendulous ears and a convex profile. It has been exported to many parts of the world, and is found in more than sixty countries. In many of them it is known simply as the Nubian.

children.name: Oberhasli
children.description: The Oberhasli is a modern American breed of dairy goat. It derives from the subtype of Chamois Colored Goat from the Oberhasli district of the Bernese Oberland in central Switzerland. All purebred members of the breed descend from five Chamois Colored Goats imported to the United States in 1936. A breeder's association was formed in 1977, and a herdbook established in the following year. Until then, goats of this type had been known as Swiss Alpine, and interbred with Alpine goats of other types.

children.name: Saanen
children.description: The Saanen is a Swiss breed of domestic goat. It takes its name from the Saanental in the Bernese Oberland, in the southern part of the Canton of Bern, in western Switzerland. It is a highly productive dairy goat and is distributed in more than eighty countries worldwide.

children.name: Toggenburg
children.description: The Toggenburger or Toggenburg is a Swiss breed of dairy goat. Its name derives from that of the Toggenburg region of the Canton of St. Gallen, where it is thought to have originated. It is among the most productive breeds of dairy goat and is distributed world-wide, in about fifty countries in all five inhabited continents.

children.name: Boer
children.description: The Boer or Boerbok is a South African breed of meat goat. It was selectively bred in the Eastern Cape from about 1920 for meat qualities and for the ability to survive by grazing on the thorn veldt of that region. It has been exported to many countries, and has been used to improve the meat qualities of other breeds.

children.name: Kiko
children.description:
The Kiko is a breed of meat goat originating from New Zealand. Kiko comes from the Māori word for meat. The Kiko breed was developed in the 1980s by Garrick and Anne Batten, who cross-bred local feral goats with imported dairy goat bucks of the Anglo-Nubian, Saanen, and Toggenburg breeds. The only aims of the breeding programme were fast rate of growth and ability to survive in the pastoral conditions of the New Zealand hill country.
The Kiko breed was imported into the United States in 1992 by Goatex Group LLC. Today, three registries exist in the US for Kikos: the AKGA, the IKGA, and the NKR, the latter of which is the largest of the three. Through these agencies, Kikos could be registered as 100% New Zealand, meaning that their lineage can be traced all the way back to the original New Zealand stock. "Purebreds" refer to goats that are at least 15/16ths New Zealand stock and "percentages" are those that are at least 50% New Zealand stock. Kiko-Boer crosses can also be registered as Genemaster™ through the NKR.

children.name: Angora
children.description: The Angora or Ankara is a Turkish breed of domesticated goat. It produces the lustrous fibre known as mohair. It is widespread in many countries of the world. Many breeds derive from it, among them the Indian Mohair, the Soviet Mohair, the Angora-Don of the Russian Federation and the Pygora in the United States.

children.name: Cashmere
children.description:
A cashmere goat is a type of goat that produces cashmere wool, the goat's fine, soft, downy, winter undercoat, in commercial quality and quantity. This undercoat grows as the days get shorter and is associated with an outer coat of coarse hair, which is present all the year and is called guard hair. Most common goat breeds, including dairy goats, grow this two-coated fleece but cashmere breeds have been selected for quality and quantity of their undercoat.
The down is produced by secondary follicles, the guard hair by the primary follicles.

children.name: Nigerian Dwarf
children.description: The Nigerian Dwarf is a modern American breed of dwarf goat. Like the American Pygmy Goat, it derives from the West African Dwarf group of breeds of West Africa.

children.name: Pygmy
children.description:
The American Pygmy is an American breed of achondroplastic (dwarf) goat. It is small, compact and stockily built. Like the Nigerian Dwarf, it derives from the West African Dwarf group of breeds of West Africa. Between 1930 and 1960, animals of this type were imported to the United States for use either as zoo animals or for research; some were later kept and bred as companion animals and established as a breed in 1975.
It may also be known as the Pygmy or African Pygmy. It is quite different and separate from the British Pygmy breed.
The goat or domestic goat (Capra hircus) is a species of goat-antelope that is mostly kept as livestock..

children.name: Capra ibex
children.description: The Alpine ibex (Capra ibex), also known as the steinbock, is a European species of goat which lives in the Alps.

children.name: Capra nubiana
children.description: The Nubian ibex (Capra nubiana) is a desert-dwelling species of goat (genus Capra) found in mountainous areas of northern and northeast Africa, and the Middle East.

children.name: Capra pyrenaica
children.description: The Iberian ibex (Capra pyrenaica), also known as the Spanish ibex, Spanish wild goat and Iberian wild goat, is a species of ibex endemic to the Iberian Peninsula.

children.name: Capra sibirica
children.description: The Siberian ibex (Capra sibirica), also known using regionalized names including Altai ibex, Asian ibex, Central Asian ibex, Gobi ibex, Himalayan ibex, Mongolian ibex, and Tian Shan ibex, is a polytypic species of ibex, a wild relative of goats and sheep.

children.name: Capra walie
children.description: The Walia ibex (Capra walie, Amharic: ዋልያ wālyā) is a vulnerable species of ibex.

children.name: Capricornis
children.description: The serows, five species of goat-antelope found in rugged mountains and forests from the Himalayas to Japan and Southeast Asia, with a distinctive gland below each eye and coarse, shaggy coats.

children.name: Capricornis crispus
children.description: The (Capricornis crispus) (羚羊) is a Japanese goat-antelope, an even-toed ungulate.

children.name: Capricornis maritimus
children.description: Capricornis maritimus (Indochinese Serow) is a serow species found in Asia region.

children.name: Capricornis milneedwardsii
children.description: The mainland serow is a species of serow native to the Himalayas, Southeast Asia and China.

children.name: Capricornis rubidus
children.description: The red serow, also called the Burmese red serow, is a goat-antelope thought to be native to southern Bangladesh and northern Myanmar. It sometimes has been considered a subspecies of C. sumatraensis.

children.name: Capricornis sumatraensis
children.description: The mainland serow is a species of serow native to the Himalayas, Southeast Asia and China.

children.name: Capricornis swinhoei
children.description: The Taiwanese serow also known as the Formosan serow, is a small species of bovid that is endemic to Taiwan.

children.name: Capricornis thar
children.description: The Himalayan serow, also known as the thar, is a subspecies of the mainland serow native to the Himalayas. It was previously considered its own species, as Capricornis thar. It is the official state animal of the Indian state of Mizoram.

children.name: Hemitragus
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Himalayan tahr, a large wild ungulate of the Himalayas with a dense reddish-brown mane and backward-curved horns, prized by hunters and widely introduced to New Zealand and South Africa.

children.name: Hemitragus jemlahicus
children.description: The Himalayan tahr is a large even-toed ungulate native to the Himalayas in southern Tibet, northern India, western Bhutan and Nepal. It is listed as Near Threatened on the IUCN Red List, as the population is declining due to hunting and habitat loss.

children.name: Naemorhedus
children.description: The gorals, four small, nimble goat-antelopes of steep rocky terrain from the Himalayas to eastern Siberia and Korea, built for life on precipitous cliffs where few other mammals can follow.

children.name: Naemorhedus baileyi
children.description: The red goral is a species of even-toed ungulate in the subfamily Caprinae in the family Bovidae. It is found in India, China (Tibet) and Myanmar. Its natural habitats are seasonal mountainous areas 1,000 to 2,000 meters above sea level.

children.name: Naemorhedus bedfordi
children.description: Naemorhedus bedfordi (Bedford's Goral) is a goral species found in Asia region.

children.name: Naemorhedus caudatus
children.description: The long-tailed goral or Amur goral is a species of ungulate of the family Bovidae found in the mountains of eastern and northern Asia, including Russia, China, and Korea. A population of this species exists in the Korean Demilitarized Zone, near the tracks of the Donghae Bukbu Line. The species is classified as endangered in South Korea, with an estimated population less than 250.

children.name: Naemorhedus evansi
children.description: The Chinese goral (Naemorhedus griseus), also known as the grey long-tailed goral or central Chinese goral, is a species of goral, a small goat-like ungulate, native to mountainous regions of Myanmar, China, India, Thailand, Vietnam, and possibly Laos.

children.name: Naemorhedus goral
children.description: The Himalayan goral (Naemorhedus goral) or gray goral is a bovid species native to the Himalayas.

children.name: Naemorhedus griseus
children.description: The Chinese goral, also known as the grey long-tailed goral or central Chinese goral, is a species of goral, a small goat-like ungulate, native to mountainous regions of Myanmar, China, India, Thailand, Vietnam, and possibly Laos. In some parts of its range, it is overhunted. The International Union for Conservation of Nature has listed it as a "vulnerable species".

children.name: Nilgiritragus
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Nilgiri tahr, an endangered wild ungulate endemic to the high shola grasslands and cliffs of India's Western Ghats, with males developing a pale saddle patch with age.

children.name: Nilgiritragus hylocrius
children.description: The Nilgiri tahr (Nilgiritragus hylocrius) is an ungulate that is endemic to the Nilgiri Hills and the southern portion of the Western Ghats in the Indian states of Tamil Nadu and Kerala.

children.name: Oreamnos
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the mountain goat, North America's highest-altitude ungulate, whose thick white coat, cloven hooves with rough pads, and stocky frame allow it to navigate near-vertical cliffs in the Rocky Mountains.

children.name: Oreamnos americanus
children.description: The mountain goat (Oreamnos americanus), also known as the Rocky Mountain goat, is a cloven-footed mammal that is endemic to the remote and rugged mountainous areas of western North America.

children.name: Ovibos
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the musk ox, a shaggy Arctic ruminant that survived the Pleistocene extinctions, bearing the world's finest natural insulating fibre (qiviut) beneath its long outer guard hairs.

children.name: Ovibos moschatus
children.description: The muskox (Ovibos moschatus) is a hoofed mammal of the family Bovidae..

children.name: Ovis
children.description: The wild and domestic sheep, around seven species from the mouflon of Mediterranean islands to the argali of Central Asian high plateaux, including the ancestor of all domestic sheep breeds first domesticated c. 11,000 years ago.

children.name: Ovis ammon
children.description: ammon Category:Mammals of Central Asia Category:Mammals of Afghanistan Category:Mammals of China Category:Mammals of Pakistan.

children.name: Ovis arabica
children.description: Ovis arabica (Arabian Mouflon) is a sheep species found in Asia region.

children.name: Ovis aries
Bluefaced Leicester
children.description: The Bluefaced Leicester is a British breed of longwool sheep. It originated in north-east England in the late nineteenth or early twentieth century, and derives from the white-faced Border Leicester, with some influence from the blue-coloured Wensleydale and possibly also from the Teeswater. It was bred specifically for use as a terminal sire to be used on ewes of hill sheep breeds to produce mules. By about 1920 it was known either as the Bluefaced or as the Hexham Leicester, for the town of Hexham in Northumberland.

children.name: Border Leicester
children.description: The Border Leicester is a British breed of sheep. It is a polled, long-wool sheep and is considered a dual-purpose breed as it is reared both for meat and for wool. It is known for its distinctive upright ears. The sheep are large but docile. They have been exported to other sheep-producing regions, including Australia and the United States.

children.name: Corriedale
children.description: The Corriedale is a New Zealand breed of sheep. It was bred from about 1882 in the South Island by James Little, who cross-bred Merino and Lincoln Longwool sheep. The breed was officially recognised in 1911. It has been exported to Australia and to many countries in Africa, Asia, Europe and North and South America. In 2021 it was reported from twenty-five countries, and the total population world-wide was estimated at just over.

children.name: Lincoln
children.description:
The Lincoln Longwool is an old British breed of sheep. It is the largest sheep of the United Kingdom, and was bred specifically for wool production. The fleece is coarse, wavy, lustrous and long, and hangs in broad staples that separate easily. The heaviest fleece on record was from a Lincoln ram.
Many were exported to other countries, particularly in the twentieth century, and the Lincoln has influenced sheep husbandry in many parts of the world, often through cross-breeding with Merino stock.

children.name: Merino
children.description:
The Merino is a breed or group of breeds of domestic sheep, characterised by very fine soft wool. It was originated in the Iberian Peninsula (modern Spain and Portugal) during the High Middle Ages, and was for several centuries kept as a strict Spanish monopoly; exports of the breed were not allowed, and those who tried risked capital punishment. During the eighteenth century, flocks were sent to the courts of a number of European countries, including France (where they developed into the Rambouillet), Hungary, the Netherlands, Prussia, Saxony and Sweden.
The Merino subsequently spread to many parts of the world, including South Africa, Australia, and New Zealand. Numerous recognised breeds, strains and variants have developed from the original type; these include, among others, the American Merino and Delaine Merino in the Americas, the Australian Merino, Booroola Merino and Peppin Merino in Oceania, and the Gentile di Puglia, Merinolandschaf and Rambouillet in Europe.

children.name: Rambouillet
children.description: The Rambouillet is a breed of sheep (Ovis aries). It is also known as the Rambouillet Merino or the French Merino.

children.name: Romney
children.description: The Romney, formerly called the Romney Marsh sheep but generally referred to by the local farmers as the Kent, is a breed of sheep originating in England. The Romney is a "long-wool" breed recognized in England by 1800. Exported to other continents, the Romney is an economically important sheep breed, especially to the sheep-meat and wool export trades of New Zealand.

children.name: Cheviot
children.description: The Cheviot is a British breed of white-faced hill sheep. It originated, and is named for, the Cheviot Hills in north Northumberland and the Scottish Borders. It is still common in this area of the United Kingdom, but also in north-west Scotland, Wales, Ireland and the south-west of England (especially Dartmoor and Exmoor), as well as more rarely in Australia, New Zealand, Norway (2%), and the United States.

children.name: Dorper
children.description: The Dorper is a South African breed of domestic sheep developed by crossing Dorset Horn and the Blackhead Persian sheep. The breed was created through the efforts of the South African Department of Agriculture to breed a meat sheep suitable to the more arid regions of the country. It is now farmed in other areas as well, and is the second most common sheep breed in South Africa.

children.name: Dorset
children.description: The Dorset Horn is an endangered British breed of domestic sheep. It is documented from the seventeenth century, and is highly prolific, sometimes producing two lambing seasons per year. Among British sheep, it is the only breed capable of breeding throughout the winter.

children.name: Hampshire
children.description: The Hampshire Down or Hampshire is a British breed of sheep. It originated in the early nineteenth century from cross-breeding of the new Southdown breed with the traditional tall, horned, white-faced sheep native to the open, untilled, chalk downland of the Hampshire Downs – the Wiltshire Horn, the Berkshire Nott and the old local Hampshire sheep. It is much used as a terminal sire.

children.name: Île-de-France
children.description:
The Île-de-France is a breed of sheep native to the French region of Île-de-France near Paris. It was first developed at a French veterinary college in the 1830s through crosses of Dishley Leicester and Rambouillet, and was originally known as the Dishley Merino. A breed association was formed in 1933, and it was rigorously tested early on its breeding for meat characteristics and maternal qualities.
Today the Île-de-France is one of the top meat breeds worldwide, and is present in South Africa, Australia and the Americas as well as in Europe. It is primarily used as a terminal sire, but is also occasionally found as a dairy breed in the United States. It's a large, naturally polled breed with white fleece.

children.name: Suffolk
children.description: The Suffolk is a British breed of domestic sheep. It originated in the late eighteenth century in the area of Bury St. Edmunds in Suffolk, as a result of cross-breeding when Norfolk Horn ewes were put to improved Southdown rams. It is a polled, black-faced breed, and is raised primarily for its meat. It has been exported to many countries, and is among the most numerous breeds of sheep worldwide.

children.name: Texel
children.description:
The Texel is a Dutch breed of domestic sheep originally from the island of Texel off the north coast of the Netherlands. It is a heavy and muscular sheep, often exhibiting extreme muscular hypertrophy, and tends to produce leaner lambs than some other breeds. It is polled, clean-faced and clean-legged, with white face and wool.
The Texel is distributed in approximately thirty-five countries in Europe, the Americas and Oceania, with estimated populations of over 5000 head in Argentina, Brazil, Chile, the Czech Republic and the United Kingdom. It is reared primarily for meat.

children.name: Awassi
children.description: The Awassi is a breed of dairy sheep of Near-Eastern fat-tailed type. It is the most widely distributed non-European dairy breed. It is known by many names, among them Arab, Baladi, Deiri, Gezirieh, Ivesi, Shami and Syrian. It is usually white with brown head and legs.

children.name: East Friesian
children.description: The Fries Melkschaap is a Dutch and German breed of dairy sheep. It originates in the Frisia region, which includes parts of both the north-eastern Netherlands and north-western Germany. It has many names: the German stock is known as the italic=no, or in English as the East Friesian, the East Friesland Milch or the German Milksheep, while the Dutch equivalent is known as the Friesian Milk or Friesian Milksheep, or less often as the Friesian or West Friesian. Under suitable management conditions, it is among the highest-yielding of dairy sheep breeds.

children.name: Lacaune
children.description: The Lacaune (Languedocien: La Cauna) is a breed of domestic sheep originating near Lacaune in southern France. The native region of these sheep is the Tarn and Aveyron departments and surrounding areas. This region is collectively known as the "Roquefort Sector" which references the milk collection area. The Lacaune is the most widely used dairying sheep breed in France, with a population of about 800,000 ewes. Notably, it is the predominant breed used in the production of Roquefort cheese in France.
Category:Mammals described in 1758 Category:Animal taxa named by Carl Linnaeus.

children.name: Ovis bochariensis
children.description: Ovis bochariensis (Bukhara Urial) is a sheep species found in Asia region.

children.name: Ovis canadensis
children.description: The bighorn sheep (Ovis canadensis) or bighorn is a species of sheep native to North America.

children.name: Ovis collium
children.description: Ovis collium (Kazakh Argali) is a sheep species found in Asia region.

children.name: Ovis cycloceros
children.description: Ovis cycloceros (Afghan Urial) is a sheep species found in Asia region.

children.name: Ovis dalli
children.description: Dall sheep or thinhorn sheep (Ovis dalli), is a species of wild sheep native to northwestern North America.

children.name: Ovis darwini
children.description: Ovis darwini (Gobi Argali) is a sheep species found in Asia region.

children.name: Ovis gmelini
children.description: The mouflon (Ovis gmelini) or moufflon is a wild sheep native to Cyprus, two separate parts of Turkey, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Georgia and Iran..

children.name: Ovis hodgsoni
children.description: Ovis hodgsoni (Tibetan Argali) is a sheep species found in Asia region.

children.name: Ovis isphahanica
children.description: The mouflon (Ovis gmelini) or moufflon is a wild sheep native to Cyprus, two separate parts of Turkey, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Georgia and Iran..

children.name: Ovis jubata
children.description: Ovis jubata (Maneed Sheep) is a sheep species found in Asia region.

children.name: Ovis karelini
children.description: Ovis karelini (Karelin's Argali) is a sheep species found in Asia region.

children.name: Ovis laristanica
children.description: The mouflon (Ovis gmelini) or moufflon is a wild sheep native to Cyprus, two separate parts of Turkey, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Georgia and Iran..

children.name: Ovis nigrimontana
children.description: Ovis nigrimontana (Kara-Tau Argali) is a sheep species found in Asia region.

children.name: Ovis nivicola
children.description: The snow sheep (Ovis nivicola), or Siberian bighorn sheep, is a species of sheep from the mountainous areas in the northeast of Siberia.

children.name: Ovis polii
children.description: Ovis polii (Marco Polo Sheep) is a sheep species found in Asia region.

children.name: Ovis punjabiensis
children.description: Ovis punjabiensis (Punjab Urial) is a sheep species found in Asia region.

children.name: Ovis severtzovi
children.description: Ovis severtzovi (Severtsov's Argali) is a sheep species found in Asia region.

children.name: Ovis vignei
children.description: The urial ( OOR-ee-əl; Ovis vignei), also known as arkars, shapo, or shapu, is a wild sheep native to Central and South Asia..

children.name: Pantholops
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the chiru (Tibetan antelope), a critically threatened high-altitude antelope of the Tibetan Plateau, whose incredibly fine underfur (shahtoosh) was once heavily poached for luxury shawls.

children.name: Pantholops hodgsonii
children.description: The Tibetan antelope or chiru (Pantholops hodgsonii) ( , pronounced ; ) is a medium-sized bovid native to the northeastern Tibetan Plateau.

children.name: Pseudois
children.description: The blue sheep (bharal), two species of Himalayan caprid intermediate in appearance between sheep and goats, whose blue-grey coats make them nearly invisible against high-altitude rocky slopes and serve as a key prey species for snow leopards.

children.name: Pseudois nayaur
children.description: The bharal (Pseudois nayaur), also called the blue sheep, is a caprine native to the high Himalayas..

children.name: Pseudois schaeferi
children.description: The bharal (Pseudois nayaur), also called the blue sheep, is a caprine native to the high Himalayas..

children.name: Rupicapra
children.description: The chamois, two species of nimble mountain goat-antelopes found in the Alps, Pyrenees, Apennines, and Caucasus, celebrated for their agility on near-vertical rock faces and seasonal coat changes from tawny to dark brown.

children.name: Rupicapra asiatica
children.description: Rupicapra asiatica (Anatolian Chamois) is a chamois species found in Asia region.

children.name: Rupicapra carpatica
children.description: Rupicapra carpatica (Carpathian Chamois) is a chamois species found in Europe region.

children.name: Rupicapra ornata
children.description: Abruzzo chamois (Rupicapra pyrenaica ornata) is a goat-antelope native to the central Apennine Mountains in central and southern Italy.

children.name: Rupicapra pyrenaica
children.description: The Pyrenean chamois (Rupicapra pyrenaica) is a goat-antelope that lives in the Pyrenees and Cantabrian Mountains of Spain, France and Andorra, and the Apennine Mountains of central Italy.

children.name: Rupicapra rupicapra
children.description: The chamois (; French: [ʃamwa] ; Rupicapra rupicapra), or Alpine chamois, is a species of goat-antelope native to mountainous parts of Europe and Western Asia, from the Pyrenees and the Cantabrian Mountain Range, the Alps, the Apennines, the Dinarides, the Tatra to the Carpathian Mountains, the Balkan Mountains, the Rila–Rhodope massif, Pindus, the northeastern mountains of Turkey, and the Caucasus..
